title: Versioned delivery, atomic swap and re-expansion
summary: Ship updates without an app release, and handle rules whose meaning changes
description:
CURRENT STATE: nothing built. Depends on the dataset format phase.

Deliver dataset updates over the air so adding a country or language is never an app release (R5, Guidelines §1).

DELIVERY: seed data ships in the app bundle so a fresh install filters offline immediately with no first-run download. Updates are fetched over the air, versioned, and verified before use. Static hosting only — no application server, which is what keeps R8's free-with-no-ads position honest.

ATOMIC SWAP: a half-applied dataset must NEVER be visible to the evaluator. A partial swap would silently evaluate rules against inconsistent data — no error, just wrong answers. Swap whole versions, never in place.

THE HARD PART — AN UPDATE CAN CHANGE WHAT A RULE MEANS. New valid lengths, a changed national pattern, or a reassigned geographic prefix all change what an existing rule expands to. Consequences:
- Rules must be RE-EXPANDED after an update.
- On iOS the Call Directory must be reloaded (CXCallDirectoryManager reloadExtensionWithIdentifier:). Prefer incremental updates (isIncremental, removeBlockingEntryWithPhoneNumber:) over full rebuilds.
- Per R2's honesty requirement, the user must be TOLD when a rule's meaning or per-platform verdict changed. A rule must never silently start or stop matching.
- A rule that fitted the iOS limit before an update may not after it, and vice versa. That transition needs a defined, visible behaviour.

This is exactly why Guidelines §2 forbids persisting expansions as rules — had expansions been stored, every update would quietly rot them.

DIAGNOSTICS: the active dataset version must be visible in the app. "Why did this rule stop matching" is otherwise unanswerable.

EDGE CASES: update interrupted mid-download; corrupt or truncated dataset; device offline for a long time then jumping several versions; an update arriving while the iOS extension is mid-run.
